property_summary: If an external call made via forward returns false then forward reverts (so a failing call cannot be observed as succeeded).
Any call to c.forward(...) always reverts (i.e., reverted == true) for all input arguments under the original contract.
The test asserts that calling c.forward(callee, _data) always reverts (reverted == true).
The test asserts that calling c.forward(callee, _data) always reverts (reverted == true).
The test asserts that calling c.forward(callee, _data) always reverts (i.e., reverted == true).

For any callee address that reverts on fallback, calling C.forward(callee, data) always reverts in the reference (require checks the call result) but the mutant that drops the require will succeed — so the reference always propagates a failing external call as a revert, whereas the mutant sometimes does not.
Calling forward with calldata that makes the callee succeed must not revert (i.e., forward should only revert when the external call actually fails).
c.forward should revert exactly when the external call returns false (i.e., reverted == !success).
c.forward reverts if and only if the low-level call to the provided callee fails, so calling c.forward on any callee that returns successfully must not revert.
Calling c.forward should revert exactly when the callee's low-level call returns false (i.e., reverted == !calleeSucceeds).
c.forward(...) always reverts when the external low-level call to callee returns false, and never reverts when it returns true (i.e., reverted == !calleeSucceeds).

For any callee that may either succeed or revert, the reference contract's forward(...) call returns (does not revert) exactly when the low-level call to callee succeeds; the mutant inverts the require so it reverts on a successful callee call (breaking this correspondence) — so the rule: forward returns iff the callee's low-level call succeeds.

Calling forward with any callee and data never leaves a stale local boolean that can later be read as false by an external observer; specifically, immediately after forward returns, a subsequent external call that queries address(c).balance unchanged implies forward did not silently fail (i.e., it reverted on failure).

Calling forward should always revert iff the low-level call to callee returns false, so for any callee/data the contract-level call either reverts or succeeds consistent with that boolean (here observed as reverted==true).
For any callee address with no code (an EOA), calling c.forward(callee, data) must not return successfully (i.e., the InvMutTest run must observe reverted == true).
forward() never returns successfully when the low-level call to callee would fail, so for addresses without code (EOAs) the call must revert (reverted == true).
For any callee/address, if callee is not a contract (no code) then calling c.forward(callee, data) must revert (i.e., reverted == true).
